# .gitattributes Explainer: which line sets this attribute, and why does my .gitattributes line do nothing?

> Free .gitattributes checker. From your attribute files (root and nested .gitattributes, .git/info/attributes, the global file) and a list of paths, it gives every attribute of every path with the file and line that decided it and the macro it came through, resolved the way `git check-attr -a` does. It flags lines git drops (`!` patterns, `[attr]` macros below the root, invalid or `builtin_` names, lines of 2,048+ bytes), `docs/` folder patterns that never reach a file, Git LFS lines without `-text`, misspelled names and values git ignores (`eol=CRLF`, `text=true`, `diff=false`, `Text`), and says per file what git does to line endings under core.autocrlf and core.eol. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded. A zero-dependency CLI runs it over a whole repository and can compare every answer with your own git (`--verify`).

Free and open source (MIT). Results come from this tool's reimplementation of git's attribute rules, checked against `git check-attr -a` and `git ls-files --eol` on random repositories and against real commits and checkouts for line endings; it is not legal, security or professional advice, and your own git is the final word. `linguist-*` attributes are read by GitHub Linguist, not git; they are resolved here the way git resolves them.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/gitattributes-explainer/)
- [Why is my .gitattributes not working? Five lines git ignores](https://marisstella.app/gitattributes-explainer/why-gitattributes-not-working.html)

## For agents

- Engine: `gitattributes.mjs`. `analyze({ sources, paths, git, settings })`: `sources` is the root .gitattributes text, or several files each introduced by a line `==> path/.gitattributes <==` (`.git/info/attributes` and `core.attributesFile` allowed); `paths` is newline-separated paths (a trailing `/` checks a folder; `git ls-files --eol` lines and C-quoted names are read) or an array of exact paths; `git` is `"modern"` (2.52+, default), `"mid"` (2.44 to 2.51) or `"old"` (2.43 or earlier); `settings` is `{ autocrlf: "false"|"true"|"input", eol: "native"|"lf"|"crlf", platform: "unix"|"windows" }`. Returns `paths` (per path `attrs`: `name`, `shown`, `rule` {source, line, text}, `via` macro chain; `eol`: `label`, `summary`, `checkout`), `findings` (severity, kind, source, line, title, detail) and `totals`. `why({ sources, path })` lists every matching line in git's reading order with what each attribute did. `DEFAULTS` is the page's example. Callable through `node platform/agents/tools.mjs call gitattributes-explainer analyze --input '{"sources":"docs/ linguist-documentation","paths":"docs/guide.md"}'` or the repository's MCP server (`call_tool`).
- CLI: `node ventures/gitattributes-explainer/cli/check.mjs` inside any git repository (`--why <path>`, `--verify`, `--json`, `--strict`, `--bundle`).
